display.purpose: Page titles, card/section titles, topbar breadcrumb — Playfair Display via inline style, always paired with a Noto Sans Thai fallback.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy, static chrome, and dense-page input/table content at the 14px content tier.

label.purpose: Buttons, form labels, status pills, secondary/fine-print text — 12px floor, never smaller for a real form label.

mono.purpose: Quotation numbers, document numbers, currency, dates, product codes — anything read character-by-character.

shadows.name: floating-panel

narrative.overview:
TCS ERP looks like the official record book of a serious trading house, not a generic SaaS dashboard. Navy is the ink and the leather binding — it is the color of authority, of a company that stores and moves chemicals for a living and can't afford ambiguity in its paperwork. Gold is used the way a ledger uses a wax seal or a gilded edge: sparingly, on the things that represent approval, action, or attention — a primary button, an active nav item, a "pending approval" pill. Playfair Display headings give every page title the weight of a printed heading in a bound register, while Inter carries the actual day-to-day reading — the paragraphs, labels, and form fields a clerk fills in dozens of times a day. JetBrains Mono marks anything that must be read exactly and never mistaken: quotation numbers, dates, currency.

The system is formal and trustworthy by necessity (it carries a server-enforced audit trail, RBAC, and approval workflow), but the mandate from the people who actually use it every day is that formal must never mean unfriendly: the ledger metaphor governs color and type, not density or tone. Screens stay legible and unintimidating — generous padding, plain-language page descriptions, one clear primary action per screen, and empty states that always say what to do next rather than just "no data." A user who has never opened a design system should still be able to find the one gold button that matters.

The system is deliberately flat and quiet at rest — surfaces are separated by a hairline navy border, not a shadow — and reserves motion/elevation for the moment something is genuinely floating above the page (a dropdown, a modal). This keeps the "ledger" feeling calm and paper-like rather than app-glossy.
keyCharacteristics: Navy-and-gold, editorial-serif headings over a clean sans-serif body — formal without being cold.
Gold is rare and meaningful: primary actions, active/selected states, "awaiting approval." Never a background color for large areas.
Flat by default (border-only surfaces); shadow appears only when something floats above the page.
No third-party component library — every control is hand-built in Tailwind to this system's exact rules.
Every workflow status (9 of them, end to end) gets its own tinted pill color — the system doubles as a legend once learned.

rules.name: The Icon Chip Tint Rule
rules.body: A small icon sitting in a rounded square (stat tiles, action-item tiles) tints its own background by appending a literal 18 hex-alpha suffix to the icon's accent color (roughly 9% opacity), with the icon itself at full accent color — a distinct notation from the Tinted Pill Rule's Tailwind /10 /20 opacity classes. Don't mix the two conventions for the same element.

rules.name: The Rare Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold covers a small fraction of any given screen — one primary button, one active nav row, one status pill at a time. Never use gold as a large background fill, a card background, or a body-text color.

rules.name: The Tinted Pill Rule
rules.body: Every status badge uses the same formula: bg-[HEX]/10 text-[HEX] border border-[HEX]/20, one dedicated hex per status. A new status must mint its own hex under this formula rather than reusing an existing status's color.

rules.name: The Two-Tier Density Rule
rules.body: On dense working pages, chrome (labels, buttons, badges, pills) sits at 12px while actual content (input values, table data, totals) sits at 14px. Bumping everything to one size erases the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Flat-Ledger Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest, separated by a border, not a shadow. Shadow (shadow-xl) is reserved exclusively for content that overlays the page — dropdowns and modals — never an in-flow card or panel.

dos: Do keep gold rare — one primary action, one active state, one status pill at a time.
Do use the tinted-pill formula for any new status or state badge.
Do pair every 'Playfair Display' inline style with the 'Noto Sans Thai' fallback.
Do keep icon-only actions discoverable at opacity-50 by default, full opacity on hover or focus-visible — never hover-only.
Do wrap every table in overflow-x-auto and make every field-pair grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2.
Do reserve shadow-xl for genuinely floating layers — everything else stays flat with a border.
donts: Don't use gold as a large background fill, a card background, or body text color.
Don't put a shadow on an in-flow card or panel.
Don't drop a real form label below 12px — text-[10px] is only for uppercase section-eyebrow labels.
Don't apply this design system to a formal reference-form print document — the reference paper form is the design authority there, not this system.
Don't reach for a drag-and-drop library for reorderable lists — use up/down arrow buttons or native HTML5 drag events.
